newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: MARTINAIR GAINS S.AFRICAN TRAFFIC RIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: MARTINAIR GAINS S.AFRICAN TRAFFIC RIGHTS.

text.p: Dutch cargo and charter airline Martinair said on Tuesday that it had gained permanent rights to fly to South Africa, according to a company statement.
The carrier has won freight traffic rights under an NV-4 permit, which enables it to operate a twice-weekly service to South Africa.
Traffic rights to Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban have been granted. There is also the possibility of being able to carry out extra flights in the peak season, the statement added.
Previously, Martinair had been granted an NV-3 permit but this restricted the movement of perishable cargo.
Martinair is jointly owned by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines and transport group Nedlloyd .
